learning_outcomes.text: At the end of the course the students will have acquired knowledge of the main circuit diagrams for signal processing used in electronics; they will know the metrics used to evaluate their performance; they will be able to analyze simple circuits to evaluate their functionality and performance; they will know circuit simulation tools and design methodologies.

The knowledge acquired by students will allow them, at the end of the course, to design simple signal acquisition and conditioning systems; they will be able to dimension amplification and filtering circuits, both using block diagrams and circuit diagrams at transistor level; they will be able to choose the most suitable circuit topologies for the problem to be solved; they will be able to simulate a circuit to verify its functionality.
At the end of the course the students will be able to carry out a comparative evaluation of both circuit and block diagram solutions in order to make the best design and development choices.

Students will be able to express themselves adequately using the appropriate terminology to describe performance specifications and technical requirements of electronic circuits. They will have acquired an appropriate technical language that allows them to communicate adequately, especially with specialist interlocutors.

Students will acquire the skills to obtain and understand the necessary technical information from datasheets, operating manuals and commercial catalogues. They will also acquire the ability to update their skills to technological developments, to understand the functioning of new circuit solutions and to adapt to new development systems.

syllabus_topics: References to the theory of circuits and elementary components (resistors, capacitors, diodes, transistors)
Circuits with capacitors (RC network, passive filters)
Circuits with diodes (half-wave rectifier, bridge rectifier, LED and photodiodes)
Circuits with operational amplifiers (inverting, non-inverting, adder, subtractor) and related non-idealities
Physical realization of logic gates: static and dynamic concepts
Architectures and operating principles of processors
Use of laboratory instruments (signal generator, oscilloscope, multimeter, power supply, breadboards)
Creation and testing of simple analog circuits based on operational amplifiers and their characterization
Notes on the design and manufacturing of printed boards
teaching_methods: Lectures with theoretical topics and exercises
Lab sessions using teaching electronic kits
assessment_rules: The complete exam consists of a written test and an oral test. The written test involves 4 analysis and/or design exercises (2 for each module) and requires a minimum score of 15/30 to access the oral test. The final grade is the arithmetic average of the scores of the two tests, expressed out of 30. For students following the course, two intermediate tests can replace the written exam, each requiring at least 15/30 to pass, and their arithmetic mean forms the final grade. Laboratory activities are evaluated through quizzes, and attendance (max 25% absences) and quiz grades can add -1 to 2 points to the final grade if it is at least 18/30. Mandatory laboratory attendance is required to pass the exam.
